Write a Python function `roman_to_int(text)` that converts a valid Roman numeral string to an integer, handling subtractive pairs such as IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `int_to_roman(n)` that converts an integer between 1 and 3999 to its Roman numeral string, using the subtractive forms IV, IX, XL, XC, CD and CM. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `group_anagrams(words)` that groups words that are anagrams of one another. Return a dictionary whose key is the word's letters sorted into alphabetical order and whose value is the list of matching words sorted alphabetically. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `two_sum(numbers, target)` that returns the two indices of values summing to `target`, as a list [i, j] with i < j. If several pairs work, return the one with the smallest i, and among those the smallest j. Return an empty list if no pair sums to the target. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `spiral_order(matrix)` that returns every element of a rectangular matrix in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left and moving right. An empty matrix returns an empty list. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `rotate_matrix(matrix)` that returns a new square matrix rotated 90 degrees clockwise, so the first row of the result is the first column of the input read from the bottom up. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `gcd_list(numbers)` that returns the greatest common divisor of a non-empty list of positive integers. A list with one element returns that element. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `count_islands(grid)` that counts the connected groups of 1s in a rectangular grid of 0s and 1s. Cells are connected only horizontally or vertically, not diagonally. An empty grid has 0 islands. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `is_anagram(a, b)` that returns True if the two strings contain the same letters in the same quantities, ignoring case and spaces. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `parse_query_string(text)` that parses a URL query string such as 'a=1&b=2' into a dictionary of string keys to string values. A key with nothing after the '=' maps to an empty string, a repeated key keeps the last value, and an empty input returns an empty dictionary. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `most_common_word(text)` that returns the most frequent word in the string, compared in lower case and split on whitespace. If several words tie, return the one that comes first alphabetically. An empty string returns an empty string. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `remove_nth_from_end(items, n)` that returns a new list with the nth element from the end removed, where n = 1 is the last element. If n is outside the list, return an unchanged copy. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `longest_word(text)` that returns the longest whitespace-separated word in the string. If several words tie for longest, return the one that appears first. An empty string returns an empty string. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `rotate_list(items, k)` that returns a new list rotated k places to the right, so the last k elements move to the front. k may be larger than the list or negative, where a negative k rotates left. An empty list returns an empty list. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `sum_nested(nested)` that returns the sum of every integer inside a list that may contain further lists, nested to any depth. A list containing no integers sums to 0. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `max_nesting_depth(text)` that returns how deeply the round brackets in the string are nested at their deepest point. The brackets are guaranteed to be balanced; a string with none returns 0. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `pascals_triangle_row(n)` that returns row n of Pascal's triangle as a list, counting from 0, so row 0 is [1] and row 1 is [1, 1]. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `invert_dict(mapping)` that returns a new dictionary with the keys and values of a dictionary of strings swapped. The values are guaranteed to be unique. An empty dictionary returns an empty dictionary. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `merge_intervals(intervals)` that merges overlapping intervals, each given as a [start, end] pair, and returns the merged list sorted by start. Intervals that merely touch at an endpoint count as overlapping. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `first_non_repeating_char(text)` that returns the first character occurring exactly once in the string. If every character repeats, or the string is empty, return an empty string. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

An empty list returns an empty list. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `merge_sorted(a, b)` that merges two lists of integers, each already sorted in ascending order, into one sorted list. Duplicates are kept. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `balanced_brackets(text)` that returns True if every (, [ and { in the string is closed by the matching bracket in the correct order. Any other character is ignored. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `longest_common_prefix(strings)` that returns the longest string that every string in the list starts with. Return an empty string if there is no common prefix or the list is empty. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `binary_search(values, target)` that returns the index of `target` in `values`, a list of distinct integers sorted in ascending order, or -1 if it is not present. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `collatz_steps(n)` that returns how many steps the Collatz sequence takes to reach 1 from a positive integer n. Each step halves an even number or replaces an odd number n with 3n + 1. `collatz_steps(1)` is 0. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `primes_up_to(n)` that returns a list, in ascending order, of every prime number less than or equal to n. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `compress_string(text)` that run-length encodes a string, so that 'aaabb' becomes 'a3b2'. Every run is written as the character followed by its count, including runs of length 1. If the encoded string is not strictly shorter than the original, return the original unchanged. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `chunk_list(items, size)` that splits a list into consecutive chunks of at most `size` elements. The last chunk may be shorter. Return an empty list if `size` is zero or negative. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `caesar_cipher(text, shift)` that shifts every letter in the string forward by `shift` places through the alphabet, wrapping around from z to a. Case is preserved and non-letters are left alone. A negative shift moves backwards. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `valid_ipv4(text)` that returns True if the string is a valid IPv4 address: exactly four parts separated by dots, each a decimal number from 0 to 255 with no leading zeros (so '0' is allowed but '01' is not). Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `digital_root(n)` that repeatedly sums the digits of a non-negative integer until one digit is left, and returns that digit. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `find_duplicates(items)` that returns, in ascending order, every integer that appears more than once in the list. Each such value appears once in the result. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `max_subarray_sum(numbers)` that returns the largest sum obtainable from any non-empty contiguous slice of a non-empty list of integers. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `moving_average(numbers, window)` that returns the average of every consecutive group of `window` values, each rounded to four decimal places. The result has len(numbers) - window + 1 entries; return an empty list if `window` is larger than the list. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `word_frequencies(text)` that returns a dictionary mapping each word in the string to how many times it appears. Words are separated by whitespace, compared in lower case, and stripped of any leading or trailing characters from .,!?;: — an empty string returns an empty dictionary. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `matrix_transpose(matrix)` that returns the transpose of a rectangular matrix given as a list of equal-length rows. An empty matrix transposes to an empty list. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `intersect_sorted(a, b)` that returns, in ascending order and without repeats, every value that appears in both lists of integers. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `longest_increasing_run(numbers)` that returns the length of the longest strictly increasing run of consecutive elements in the list. An empty list returns 0. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `title_case_words(text)` that capitalises the first letter of every whitespace-separated word and lower-cases the rest, joining the words with a single space and no leading or trailing space. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `count_substring(text, needle)` that counts how many times `needle` occurs in `text` without overlapping, scanning left to right. An empty needle returns 0. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `sum_of_digits_in_string(text)` that adds up every digit character in the string and returns the total, ignoring every other character. A string with no digits returns 0. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `remove_duplicates_preserving_order(items)` that returns a list keeping only the first occurrence of each integer, in the order those first occurrences appeared. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.

Write a Python function `is_perfect_square(n)` that returns True if the non-negative integer n is the square of an integer. 0 is a perfect square. Return the complete function definition; you may define helper functions alongside it.
